To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of duplicate structures in the scene causes ambiguities in the structure from motion (SF) reconstruction and that these ambiguities can be disambiguated by coupling an expectation maximization-based algorithm that estimates camera positions and identifies false match-pairs and an efficient sampling method that discovers plausible data association hypotheses.

(i) the presence of multiple instances of the structure in the scene causes geometric ambiguities that can only be disambiguated by incorporating image information, and (ii) a sampling-based algorithm that uses geometric and image cues to generate data association hypotheses can be used in conjunction with an EM algorithm to recover the correct data association.

1) The problem of structure from motion with large duplicate structures is not a geometric problem, but a combinatorial problem; and 2) The combinatorial problem can be solved by coupling geometric reasoning with image-based sampling and expectation maximization.

the following questions: (1) how to identify false match-pairs and (2) how to discover correct match-pairs.
